tldr: No direct Canadian competitor moves today except BMO's quantum-computing claim. The more relevant signals are agentic checkout (Klarna x Adyen), Google Wallet's iOS launch and Nasdaq's 23/5 trading hub. Brazil and LatAm news is mostly Black Friday card offers, fee changes and Nubank's push to become a licensed bank.
themes: Card rewards and Black Friday promotions
Fee and benefit tightening (Mercado Bitcoin, Mercado Pago, Bradesco, Itaú)
Fintechs moving toward bank charters (Nubank, OakNorth)

highlights.headline: Klarna is now payable when an AI agent checks out for shoppers via Adyen Agentic.
highlights.why: Payments are moving toward agent-initiated purchases, so we should consider how our cards, wallets and credentials would work when an AI agent, not the customer, pays.

highlights.headline: Nasdaq published a 23/5 Trading Information Hub.
highlights.why: Near-round-the-clock trading is becoming a formal exchange offering, which could raise customer expectations for extended-hours access on our direct investing platform.

highlights.headline: Google Wallet launched on iOS across the US.
highlights.why: It adds a cross-platform wallet option on iPhone and could shift expectations for in-wallet cards, tickets and passes; we should check our own wallet and provisioning experience.

highlights.headline: BMO claims a quantum computing breakthrough, saying it could help AI models find the most relevant information in complex datasets.
highlights.why: BMO is the only Canadian bank in today's feed, and it is positioning itself as an AI and data innovator. We should watch whether that shows up in customer-facing features.
